On a GIL build, or when only one CPU is available to\nthe process, :func:`pmap` is exactly the sequential list comprehension it\nreplaces, so results, exceptions and side-effect order are unchanged.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport threading\nfrom concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor\n\n__all__ = ['pmap']\n\n_executor = None\n_executor_lock = threading.Lock()\n_worker_state = threading.local()\n\n\ndef _gil_enabled():\n    check = getattr(sys, '_is_gil_enabled', None)\n    return True if check is None else check()\n\n\ndef _available_cpus():\n    try:\n        return len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))\n    except (AttributeError, OSError):  # pragma: no cover - platform specific\n        return os.cpu_count() or 1\n\n\n_nworkers = None\n\n\ndef _threads_usable():\n    global _nworkers\n    if _nworkers is None:\n        _nworkers = _available_cpus()\n    return _nworkers > 1 and not _gil_enabled()\n\n\ndef _get_executor():\n    global _executor\n    if _executor is None:\n        with _executor_lock:\n            if _executor is None:\n                _executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(\n                    max_workers=_nworkers,\n                    thread_name_prefix='sympy-pmap',\n                    initializer=_mark_worker)\n    return _executor\n\n\ndef _mark_worker():\n    _worker_state.active = True\n\n\ndef _in_worker():\n    return getattr(_worker_state, 'active', False)\n\n\ndef pmap(func, items):\n    \"\"\"\n    Return ``[func(x) for x in items]``, evaluating the calls concurrently\n    when the interpreter runs free-threaded and more than one CPU is\n    available.\n\n    Results are returned in input order.  If several calls raise, the\n    exception of the earliest item is re-raised, as the sequential\n    comprehension would do. On a GIL build, or when only one CPU is available to\nthe process, :func:`pmap` is exactly the sequential list comprehension it\nreplaces, so results, exceptions and side-effect order are unchanged.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport threading\nfrom concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor\n\n__all__ = ['pmap']\n\n_executor = None\n_executor_lock = threading.Lock()\n_worker_state = threading.local()\n\n\ndef _gil_enabled():\n    check = getattr(sys, '_is_gil_enabled', None)\n    return True if check is None else check()\n\n\ndef _available_cpus():\n    try:\n        return len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))\n    except (AttributeError, OSError):  # pragma: no cover - platform specific\n        return os.cpu_count() or 1\n\n\n_nworkers = None\n\n\ndef _threads_usable():\n    global _nworkers\n    if _nworkers is None:\n        _nworkers = _available_cpus()\n    return _nworkers > 1 and not _gil_enabled()\n\n\ndef _get_executor():\n    global _executor\n    if _executor is None:\n        with _executor_lock:\n            if _executor is None:\n                _executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(\n                    max_workers=_nworkers,\n                    thread_name_prefix='sympy-pmap',\n                    initializer=_mark_worker)\n    return _executor\n\n\ndef _mark_worker():\n    _worker_state.active = True\n\n\ndef _in_worker():\n    return getattr(_worker_state, 'active', False)\n\n\ndef pmap(func, items):\n    \"\"\"\n    Return ``[func(x) for x in items]``, evaluating the calls concurrently\n    when the interpreter runs free-threaded and more than one CPU is\n    available.\n\n    Results are returned in input order.  If several calls raise, the\n    exception of the earliest item is re-raised, as the sequential\n    comprehension would do.  Calls made from inside a worker run\n    sequentially so that nested use cannot deadlock the pool.\n    \"\"\"\n    items = list(items)\n    if len(items) < 2 or _in_worker() or not _threads_usable():\n        return [func(x) for x in items]\n\n    executor = _get_executor()\n    futures = [executor.submit(func, x) for x in items]\n    results = []\n    error = None\n    for fut in futures:\n        try:\n            results.append(fut.result())\n        except BaseException as exc:\n            if error is None:\n                error = exc\n            results.append(None)\n    if error is not None:\n        raise error\n    return results\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01KYpjVMhzriDNLiMPL39WJM","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CghKNPkQf2CFTRNKXJTwy","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I did not reach the performance targets, and the submitted package is essentially the original. The only change left in `/app/sympy` is a lock around the `Dummy` index counter in `core/symbol.py`. That counter is incremented with `+=` on the free-threaded build, so two threads could get the same index, and equal indices make distinct dummy symbols compare equal. That alone exceeds the `T_1 <= 1.05 * T_original` budget, so single-thread work would need to get faster too.\n\n**What I tried and reverted**\n- I parallelized the per-entry `expand_mul`/`collect`/`doit` steps and the unique integral evaluations, with an exact-match memo for the final `doit` pass. On a 3-state case this went from 0.049 s to 0.028 s at 4 cores, and it was faster on one core as well.\n- My output comparison did not hold up. The unmodified reference differs from itself across processes because of hash randomization, so I can't claim the parallel version changed any output. Reordering evaluation can still change sympy's cache-dependent output forms, and I did not finish verifying that it doesn't. I reverted it rather than submit something unverified.\n\n**Verification status**\n- The reverted package (plus the lock) matches the reference byte-for-byte on the GIL build with `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` across 40 generated `dsolve`/`linodesolve` cases.\n- The unmodified reference itself differs between the GIL and free-threaded builds at a later case under the same seed, so exact cross-runtime comparison is not even reliable for the original library.\n- `public_check.py` runs on `python-ft` and reports GIL disabled.\n\n**Not done:** I did not verify the 1.10/1.05 scaling requirements on the final package, because there is no parallel code in it.
